newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia govt borrowing programme A$10.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia govt borrowing programme A$10.2 bln.

text.p: The Australian government's total borrowing programme for 1996/97 has been revised up to around A$10.2 billion from the A$7.0 billion planned in the August budget, the Australian Treasury said on Wednesday.

The revision followed the government's Mid-Year Economic review released Tuesday which showed a headline budget deficit of A$2.7 billion was now expected for the year to end-June 1997 against the initial forecast of a A$500 million surplus.
The revised debt issuance programme comprised Treasury Fixed Coupon Bond issuance of A$8 to A$9 billion, representing an increase of A$2 billion from budget time.
Furthermore, there would be no change in the volume of Treasury Notes on issue on a year to year basis which would be around A$1 billion higher than planned at budget time.
Treasury Indexed Bond issuance would stay at around A$500 million to A$1 billion and Treasury Adustable Bond issuance would also be unchanged from budget time at A$1 billion.

The Treasury said fixed coupon bond issuance had raised A$4.8 billion in the year to date, implying further issuance of around A$3 to A$4 billion. It was anticipated tenders would continue to be held at four to six week intervals.
Treasury said it was not envisaged that any further new benchmark lines would be introduced during the remainder of the financial year.
Treasury said the revised mid-year estimates implied a net Commonwealth borrowing requirement of A$3.9 billion for 1996/97 compared with an estimate at budget time of A$700 million.
This was made up of the headline budget deficit of A$2.7 billion and A$1.2 billion in payments associated with Commonwealth public trading enterprise superannuation.
The gross borrowing requirement also included the refinancing of A$5.3 billion of maturing debt and possible repurchase of A$1.0 billion of Treasury Bonds scheduled for maturity in budget out-years.
Treasury indexed bond issuance in the year to date had raised around A$370 million and further issuance would comprise both the 2020 line and 2015 line, Treasury said.
Treasury Adjustable Rate bonds had raised around A$300 million and further issuance wuld be directed into the existing October 2000 line.

The volume of Treasury notes on issue was around A$17.2 billion compared with A$15.8 billion at the end of June 1996. The expectation of no change in year-on-year levels thus implied a reduction in the volume of notes outstanding, Treasury said.
The Commonwealth would continue to maintain a small core holding of U.S. dollar exposure in the debt portfolio which required new US$ exposure of around A$3 billion, Treasury said.
At present the approach of issuing in the domestic market and swapping was the most cost-effective approach to acquiring this foreign currency exposure.
Although not currently planned, a return to direcrt issuance in offshore markets by the Commonwealth remained an option, Treasury added.
